title: Ebro & Peter Rosenberg Aren’t Buying Ye’s ‘Comeback’ Narrative After Antisemitism: ‘It’s All Marketing’
summary: West had more than 83,000 fans attend his AT&T Stadium show in Dallas over the weekend.
body: Ye (formerly Kanye West ) has been selling out stadiums across the globe with spot tour dates throughout 2026, most recently packing more than 83,000 fans into AT&T Stadium in Dallas for a show over the weekend. Ebro Darden and Peter Rosenberg debated the merits of West’s touring in 2026 on Monday’s (Nov. 9) episode of The Ebro Laura Rosenberg Show , and the media personalities aren’t buying the comeback narrative tied to Ye following his antisemitic remarks and controversial antics in years past. title: Young Thug and Birdman Dismissed From Lawsuit Over 2015 Lil Wayne Tour Bus Shooting
summary: The shooting was cited as part of the sweeping YSL gang prosecution in Atlanta, in which Thug ultimately walked free.
body: After a decade of litigation, Young Thug and Birdman have triumphed over legal claims that sought to hold them liable for a shooting on Lil Wayne ’s tour bus in Atlanta. Two Georgia court orders on Tuesday (Nov. 10), obtained by Billboard , dismissed Thug (Jeffrey Williams) and Birdman (Bryan Williams) from the lawsuit filed back in 2016 by Wayne’s former tour bus driver, Alvin Lewis. The driver still has civil claims for emotional damages pending against two other men over the 2015 shooting, a drive-by that occurred on the I-285 freeway after Wayne performed at The Compound club in Atlanta. title: Google Wallet adds digital home keys to open your front door smart lock with a tap
summary: There's hands-free unlocking too!
body: TL;DR Google Wallet is gaining digital home keys, allowing Android users to unlock compatible smart locks with an NFC tap or hands-free using UWB. The feature supports select Aliro-compatible locks from Aqara, Schlage, and Nuki, with one digital key working across multiple locks in the same home. The functionality is rolling out to Google Home Public Preview users starting today, November 11, with wider availability expected over the coming weeks. Smart locks have already made getting into homes a lot more convenient than it traditionally used to be, and Google is now making that process even more seamless by bringing digital home keys directly into Google Wallet . Starting today, those in the Google Home app’s Public Preview will have the option to add their digital home keys to Google Wallet, allowing compatible smart lock owners to unlock doors by simply walking up to it or tapping their phones against the lock.

title: Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 gives your old speakers and TVs a second life for $69
summary: That forgotten hi-fi system isn't ready for retirement.
body: TL;DR Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 brings older speakers, TVs, and other compatible electronics into the modern smart home. It supports lossless audio, local device control, Bluetooth connectivity, and Z-Wave adapters. The new accessory is available starting November 11 for $69 in the US and €59 in Europe. Not every device needs replacing just because it missed the smart home revolution. That old stereo gathering dust might still sound better than your shiny new wireless speaker , while your TV or heating system could be perfectly capable of following commands without an internet connection. Home Assistant wants to bridge that gap with a new accessory that gives yesterday’s technology a place in today’s connected home. The new Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 is a multi-purpose accessory from Nabu Casa, the company behind official Home Assistant hardware. Rather than adding yet another gadget to your home, Connect AUX-2 is designed to make better use of the ones you already own, bringing older audio systems, TVs, solar equipment, and more into an existing Home Assistant setup.

title: YouTube TV channels are missing from Google TV live tab for some users (Updated)
summary: This is not the first time the problem has cropped up.
body: TL;DR YouTube TV channels are missing from the live tab in Google TV Live Guide for some users. The issue has shown up on Google TVs, Chromecasts, and third-party Google TV streaming devices. This is not the first time the problem has occurred, but so far there is no word from Google about when it will be fixed. Update, November 11, 2026 (4:04 PM ET): Google has responded to our inquiry and tells Android Authority , “we are aware of the issue, and it has now been fixed.” Hopefully everyone affected is now seeing their YouTube TV channels back where they belong. Original article, November 11, 2026 (3:25 PM ET): YouTube TV channels have disappeared from their usual spot in the Live tab on the Google TV Live Guide on Google TVs and Chromecast devices. title: Google brings the standalone Gemini app and Gemini Live to Apple CarPlay

body: TL;DR Google is rolling out a standalone Gemini app to Apple CarPlay globally, bringing Gemini Live to the platform. Unlike its existing Google Maps integration, the standalone app supports broader conversations and Workspace integration. The rollout begins today, November 11. Users need the latest Gemini app on their iPhone and must have used Gemini Live at least once. Google is expanding its AI presence on Apple CarPlay by bringing the standalone Gemini app to the platform starting today, Wednesday, November 11. For reference, CarPlay users have already been able to leverage Gemini’s smarts, albeit only in Maps . The development today takes things a step further. The new standalone app brings access to Gemini Live too, unlocking hands-free conversational assistance throughout your rides. The move has been a long time coming, especially considering that AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Copilot are already available on CarPlay.

title: Google Lens bug traps Chrome users by hiding the close button
summary: Google says the bug is fixed, but some users are still stuck.
body: TL;DR Google Lens has not been letting Chrome users close out of the side panel. The problem appears to lie with a CSS issue from a Chrome update to the Lens overlay. Google said the issue is fixed but some people still have the issue even after the latest update. Google Lens , the AI-powered search tool that lets you find what you’re looking for with images instead of words, has not been letting Chrome users close out of the feature. That should now be fixed, according to Google, though not everyone affected seems to agree. Reports on Reddit and Google’s Chrome Help Support forums started coming in about a week ago: The “x” to close out of Google Lens was missing for many. None of the usual fixes — closing tabs, shutting Chrome altogether, clearing cache and cookies, and restarting computers — worked to rectify the situation. One user who replied to a post in a Chrome sub shared a temporary solution to closing out of Lens: dragging the tab with Lens open into a new window and then dragging it back into the old window.

title: Garmin launches 5 US Armed Forces watch faces for veterans and military families
summary: New designs honor five US military branches.
body: TL;DR Garmin has launched five new watch faces featuring the official logos of the US Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, and Space Force. The designs are available through Connect IQ for select fēnix, Instinct, tactix, Forerunner, and other Garmin smartwatches. A portion of sales proceeds will support programs for military personnel, veterans, and their families. Garmin has long catered to people who spend more time navigating rugged terrain than browsing smartwatch apps. Its military-inspired tactix lineup and rugged Instinct watches are built for demanding environments, with some models offering specialized features such as stealth mode and night-vision compatibility. But not everyone with a connection to the military needs those tactical tools. Sometimes, a little service pride on the wrist is enough. Just in time for Veterans Day, Garmin is giving military personnel, veterans, and their supporters another way to make their smartwatches their own. The company has introduced a collection of five watch faces featuring the official logos of the US Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, and Space Force.

title: Google Home bug leaves Nest camera notifications without video previews
summary: You're not alone if your Nest camera notifications are text-only.
body: TL;DR Nest camera users report missing video previews and thumbnails in Android notifications. The issue affects multiple phones and Nest camera models, though previews still work on some other devices. Cameras continue recording normally; it’s just the previews that are missing. We’ve reached out to Google for clarification. Nest camera users are reporting a frustrating bug that’s causing video previews and thumbnails on Android to disappear from notifications. This is leaving users who have gotten in the habit of quickly glancing over their camera feeds through previews with no choice but to open the Google Home app. For those unaware, Google Home’s camera notifications include a thumbnail or a short video preview to highlight what triggered the alert. This makes it easier to determine whether the alert was triggered by something routine or something that needs more attention via the Google Home app. With previews now missing , users are being forced to default to the latter option.

body: TL;DR The latest version of the Google Voice app includes multiple clues about RCS messaging support. Google Voice currently supports only standard SMS and MMS across all plans, contrasting with some of Google’s own apps. It’s still too early to say when RCS support will be officially enabled in Google Voice, but these are encouraging signs. Popular VoIP app Google Voice is laying the groundwork for RCS (Rich Communication Services) messaging, we can exclusively reveal. Google Voice users are currently limited to standard SMS and MMS, a glaring limitation at a time when multiple apps, including Google Messages, already support RCS messaging. body: TL;DR The Pixel Journal app is taking early steps toward letting users add audio recordings through a Google Recorder integration. We’re also seeing references in the app that mention adding existing voice recordings and transcripts. The Pixel-exclusive journaling app is also adding a new export option to back up all contents in a zip file. An update to the Pixel Journal app shows early signs of the upcoming Google Recorder integration and adds a nifty export option for your entries. title: GrapheneOS for Pixel 11 is almost here, and there’s encouraging news for performance
summary: GrapheneOS on Pixel 11 phones could have similar performance as other Pixels.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR The team behind GrapheneOS has confirmed that a port of the OS to Pixel 11 phones is almost complete. They add that Pixel 11 support will be available after the Motorola Signature 27 gets GrapheneOS. The group further notes that GrapheneOS on Pixel 11 phones delivers performance that’s “more than good enough.” GrapheneOS is arguably the best Android fork if you value security and privacy. The software originally missed Pixel 11 phones because they lacked support for the Memory Tagging Extensions (MTE) feature. However, MTE is shipping to Pixel 11 devices with Android 17 QPR2, and the team has now revealed more details about the port. The GrapheneOS team announced on social media that GrapheneOS for Pixel 11 phones was nearly complete. Furthermore, the group said that GrapheneOS based on Android 17 QPR2 indeed supports MTE functionality. There’s no specific release window just yet, but the team explains that Pixel 11 support will “soon” be added after the Motorola Signature 27 gets the OS and following the completion of GrapheneOS based on Android 17 QPR2.

The change applies to Android 11 and newer and covers edits made with tools like Magic Eraser and Unblur, as well as Ultra HDR and C2PA photos. Once the change goes into effect, you’ll no longer be able to log into your Nintendo account with a Google or Apple account. You could even do this with your Nintendo account, but that will no longer be the case soon. Nintendo is putting an end to linking your account with Google or Apple accounts. A newly published support page reveals that Nintendo plans on discontinuing Google and Apple account linking. Once the change goes into effect, you’ll no longer be able to log into your Nintendo account with a Google or Apple account. Users are also losing the ability to create a Nintendo account using Google or Apple. Additionally, the game publisher is putting an end to the My Nintendo Platinum Points mission that rewards users for connecting their accounts.

title: Pixel 11’s better Pixel Search is expanding to every Pixel launched since 2021
summary: That includes phones as old as the Pixel 6, including even the A-series ones.
body: Credit: Prakhar Khanna / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s Pixel Search app, launched with the Pixel 11, is coming to older phones. All phones, including Pixel 6 and newer, now support the refreshed Search experience. Pixel Search goes beyond traditional Google Search on Android devices, letting users look for files, folders, conversations, Drive, Photos, calendar entries, and more using natural language. The November 2026 Pixel Drop is here, and along with several new features for the broad Pixel lineup, it also expands Pixel 11-exclusive items to older phones. One such feature is the renewed Pixel Search experience , which first arrived with the Pixel 11 series. Now, Google is expanding it to older phones, going all the way back to the Pixel 6 series. The persistent search bar on Pixel phones’ home screens has long offered an experience that is distinct from the rest of Android devices. Unlike other Android devices, search on Pixel phones has traditionally also brought up results from local files and apps alongside web search results. Last year, Google temporarily took that away , but only to introduce an even more far-reaching Pixel Search app when it launched the Pixel 11 phone…

title: Google’s November Pixel Drop brings over 12 new features, and Pixel 10 owners are the big winners
summary: Pixel Solver, Create My Widget, and Gemini Call Screen lead the way, while Pixel 10 owners finally get Gemini Intelligence.
body: Google has announced its November Pixel Drop, and this time, it’s a busy one. The update starts rolling out today, November 10, to all supported Pixel phones, tablets, and smartwatches. It brings a handful of genuinely new tools, including an AI-powered math solver in the Calculator app and a long-awaited widget builder that works from natural language prompts. Pixel Tag, first announced alongside the Pixel 11 series, is also now officially available. Meanwhile, Pixel 10 owners are getting a big chunk of the Gemini Intelligence features that launched with the Pixel 11 series , including Rambler and Gemini’s task automations. Several other features are also expanding to older Pixels and new regions.

title: Google rolls out Create My Widget to Pixel 10 and 11 series, but the Pixel 10a misses out
summary: You can now use natural language commands to generate widgets, but not on the budget Pixel.
body: Credit: Play Store TL;DR Google is rolling out the Create My Widget generative AI tool to Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series via the November 2026 Pixel Feature Drop. The feature generates Material-style home screen widgets from natural-language text prompts, but notably excludes the Pixel 10a. Google confirmed that Create My Widget is also coming soon to the Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 in select regions. Google’s November 2026 Pixel Feature Drop is officially here, bringing one of the most anticipated personalization tools to your Pixel: Create My Widget. Google announced Create My Widget earlier this year, and is now formally rolling out the generative AI tool to help users design personalized home screen widgets tailored to their everyday needs and workflow. Until now, Create My Widget was surprisingly exclusive to Googlebook laptops , remaining conspicuously absent on Android/Pixel despite a brief sighting through a Google Play Store listing . With the November 2026 Pixel Feature Drop update, rolling out starting today, Pixel users can finally build their own widgets by choosing from curated suggestions or typing simple natural-language prompts.

title: Pixel phones are getting 10 new custom icon styles
summary: Google’s November Pixel Drop adds 10 new custom icon styles.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Google is rolling out new custom icon styles as part of the November Pixel Drop. The update adds 10 new styles to choose from. These new icon styles are available for the Pixel 6a and above. One of the more overlooked features included in the March 2026 Pixel Drop was custom icons . This feature gave you more customization options for dressing up your home screen. However, Google initially only offered six styles to choose from. If you have been using the feature, then you’ll be glad to know that it is getting an expansion. As part of the November 2026 Pixel Drop, Google is adding new custom icon styles. Overall, you’re getting 10 more styles to play around with. That brings the number of available options up from six to a total of 16.

title: Pixel’s Notification Summaries are coming to the Pixel Watch 3 and newer
summary: But only if you use Pixel 9 or a newer Google phone.
body: Credit: Andy Boxall / Android Authority TL;DR Your Pixel Watch 3 or newer can now summarize your notifications for you. After bringing AI-powered notification summaries to the Pixel phones last year, Google is expanding them to the Pixel Watch. To be able to use it, your Watch must be connected to a Pixel 9 or newer phone running at least Android 16.1. With the November 2026 Pixel Drop , Google is bringing a host of new features to the Pixel devices. While phones get the larger share of the pie, Google is also bringing a few new features to its wearables, especially the Pixel Watch. One of those is Notification Summaries, which we already loved when we first tried it on the Pixel 10 earlier this year. Last November, Google brought AI-curated notification summaries to the Pixel 9 and newer devices, several months after we first learned the feature was in development . For those of us who tend to take a peek at our smartwatches instead of pulling the phone out every time it buzzes, notification summaries on the Pixel Watch can be a blessing.

title: Your Pixel Watch is getting a new Step-by-step Workouts feature, and it’s pretty handy
summary: Your Pixel Watch now has a workout plan, so what's your excuse?
body: TL;DR Google’s November Pixel Drop is rolling out with new features for supported Pixel phones, tablets, and smartwatches. The new Step-by-step Workouts feature is coming to the Pixel Watch 3 and newer models. It lets users follow workout instructions, log reps and weights, and track fitness metrics directly from their watch or phone. Google’s November Pixel Drop is here , and there’s plenty to unpack. The update starts rolling out today, bringing several new features to supported Pixel phones , tablets, and smartwatches. While some Pixel Drops are mostly small improvements, this one adds a few features worth getting excited about. One of the more interesting additions is coming to the Pixel Watch 3 and newer models. Google is introducing Step-by-step Workouts, a feature that could make tracking your gym sessions a lot easier.

title: Google expands Gemini Intelligence and Proactive Gemini Actions with November Pixel Drop
summary: Pixel 10 is getting Pixel 11's Gemini Intelligence, automations, and smart suggestions.
body: TL;DR Google’s November Pixel Drop brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10 series, including Rambler, personalized suggestions, and expanded automations. Rambler cleans up voice dictation, while Gemini can now handle more multi-step tasks like ordering groceries, booking rides, and making restaurant reservations. Proactive Gemini Actions adds contextual text summaries, Google Keep grocery list integration, and wider global availability. Ever tried dictating a message, only to spend the next minute deleting all the “ums,” fixing awkward sentences, and wondering whether typing would’ve been faster? Or wished you could simply tell your phone to sort out dinner instead of hopping between apps? Google wants Gemini to take both headaches off your hands, and its latest Pixel Drop is bringing more of that convenience to older Pixel phones. The November Pixel Drop is rolling out today, bringing Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold. The expansion brings several capabilities already available on the Pixel 11 series to Google’s previous-generation flagships, including Rambler , personalized suggestions, and expanded automation features.

title: Reddit Reviews want to turn user discussions into easily digestible product reviews
summary: Bringing user discussions about popular products under one roof.
body: TL;DR Reddit has introduced Reddit Reviews, an AI-powered shopping tool that turns community discussions into dedicated product reviews. Reviews include AI-generated summaries, user sentiment, product comparisons, and links to original discussions. Businesses can’t pay for product placements. The feature is rolling out on Android, iOS, and the web in the US, initially covering around 10,000 products, with international expansion planned for 2027. After announcing its transition to a split home feed layout , drawing criticism for its upcoming logged-in-only experience, and even testing ads on the search results page , Reddit is now leveraging its vast collection of real-world user discussions to launch Reddit Reviews. Yes, the feature does exactly what it sounds like. It’s a shopping tool that turns product conversations from across Reddit into dedicated reviews.

title: Google Fi’s new Super Network brings automatic 5G switching, Pixel deals, and more
summary: Bad 5G signal? Your Pixel might have a clever escape plan.
body: TL;DR Google Fi’s new Super Network lets supported Pixel phones automatically switch between two major US 5G networks for better connectivity. Network switching initially works only on Pixel 9 and newer phones using eSIM, while Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ is expanding to select Samsung and Motorola devices. Google is introducing an AI-powered assistant called Ask Fi, along with Pixel 11 offers and discounts on select Google Fi plans. Most of us choose a mobile carrier based on its coverage, data speeds, and pricing. But even the best networks have their weak spots, and there’s usually not much you can do when your phone struggles to find a decent signal. What if your phone could connect to another carrier whenever that happens? That’s exactly what Google Fi is trying to do with its new Google Fi Super Network. The service is bringing back automatic network switching, giving supported phones access to two major US 5G networks instead of relying on just one.

title: Ring is launching a flying security camera to patrol your home
summary: Ring’s flying security camera is making a comeback.
body: Credit: Amazon TL;DR Ring has announced the Ring Drone Cam, a flying indoor security camera. The drone can fly to where an incident is triggered, record in light and dark environments, and capture video in 2K resolution. Shipping starts on January 27, 2027, for $249.99. In 2020, Amazon held a hardware event where it announced several new products. Outside of the usual Echo devices, Fire TV products, and eero routers, there was a more outlandish piece of hardware called the Ring Always Home Cam . This was a mini drone that would patrol your home and send video to your phone. While that specific concept never got off the ground, Ring is now actually launching a flying camera that will go on sale. Today, Ring announced the launch of Ring Robotics, a new category of autonomous security products. To christen the launch of this new product category, the company has debuted a device called the Ring Drone Cam. Similar to the Always Home Cam, this is a small drone that patrols your home and neatly tucks away into a dock when it’s unneeded.

title: A Google TV Ambient Mode issue is causing repetitive photo slideshows and frozen screens
summary: Rolling back recent updates appears to fix the problem.
body: TL;DR Some Google TV owners are experiencing repetitive Google Photos slideshows and freezing in Ambient Mode. The problem affects Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer devices, although it doesn’t appear to affect everyone. Uninstalling Ambient Mode updates restores normal photo slideshows for some affected devices. Google TV can turn your idle screen into a digital photo frame, bringing your favorite memories to the biggest screen in the house. Google even spruced up the experience earlier this year with dynamic slideshows that transform ordinary photos into colorful collages. But for some users, that personal touch has become a frustrating exercise in repetition, with Ambient Mode recycling the same handful of pictures before freezing altogether. The complaints are piling up on Reddit , where Chromecast with Google TV owners report seeing the same photos repeatedly despite having a much larger library. Clearing Ambient Mode’s cache temporarily loads a different batch, but the cycle quickly begins again.

title: It’s official: Samsung Gallery now uses your Google storage to sync your photos and videos
summary: Samsung's OneDrive replacement is Google.
body: TL;DR Samsung has officially announced that its Gallery app can now sync photos and videos to users’ Google account storage. It lets you view synced photos and videos across Galaxy devices. The feature is rolling out to select Galaxy devices running One UI 9, and will roll out to more devices in phases. Samsung’s partnership with Microsoft OneDrive ended in late September , leaving a pretty big gap in Samsung Gallery’s cloud backup capabilities. Although we already knew the company was going to partner with Google for cloud storage, that’s now getting officially confirmed. Samsung today announced Gallery sync with Google storage to make it easier for users to back up their photos to the cloud and access them from anywhere. The sync feature works inside the Gallery app using your Samsung and Google accounts. That means if you’re already signed in with your Samsung and Google accounts on your device, you can just turn on the sync feature and start backing up your photos and videos.

summary: Your Galaxy phone will soon understand your ramblings.
body: TL;DR Samsung Keyboard could get an AI-powered feature called “Refine Voice Input” with One UI 9.5. It’s expected to work like Gboard’s Rambler voice mode, cleaning up your dictations into formatted text. It will reportedly be accessible via a Galaxy AI button on the keyboard or the side button on supported Galaxy phones. The One UI 9.5 leaks just keep on coming. We’ve already seen reports of a call recorder upgrade coming with One UI 9.5, and now another leak suggests what might be a nifty little feature for the Samsung Keyboard. According to a report from SamMobile , an internal test build of the Samsung Keyboard app includes a new option called “Refine Voice Input.” The feature description says it’s meant to “clean up filler words, hesitations, and more.” That’s pretty much what Gboard’s Rambler feature does, too.

title: Switch 2’s Zelda remake runs on Android days after launch, but you’ll need a lot of RAM
summary: Early tests show the game reaching 30fps on flagship phones, but keep your expectations grounded.
body: Credit: Oliver Cragg / Android Authority TL;DR Nintendo’s newly released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake for Switch 2 is already booting and running on Android via the BananaNative translation layer. Testers managed to achieve 25-30fps on a Snapdragon 8 Elite phone (POCO F7 Ultra) using custom GPU drivers and frame generation. The build demands more than 12GB of RAM during heavy transitions, leading to immediate crashes on phones with less than 16GB of RAM. The emulation scene has been moving very fast lately, but some recent breakthroughs border on ridiculous. Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake a few days ago for the Switch 2, and developers have already gotten it booting and running on Android, building on the rapid rise of Nintendo Switch 2 emulators and ports on Android . While we have previously seen projects bring classic Zelda titles like Majora’s Mask and the original Ocarina of Time to Android via native recompilation, having a brand-new, current-gen console remake running on mobile devices within days of release is rather unprecedented. As shown across community threads on Reddit, early builds of the game are running on high-end And…

title: Waze’s new Garmin-powered feature could make roads a lot safer for cyclists
summary: Cyclists can now make their presence known without ringing a bell.
body: TL;DR Waze and Garmin have partnered to introduce real-time cyclist alerts that help drivers spot cyclists nearby. Cyclists with compatible Garmin Edge bike computers or smartwatches can enable LiveTrack to appear on Waze and alert nearby drivers. The feature is optional, protects cyclists’ identities and routes, and is rolling out globally on Android and iOS. If you use Waze regularly , you probably know how handy its alerts can be. Whether it’s a car stopped on the side of the road, an accident ahead, or an unexpected pothole, getting a heads-up before you reach it can make driving a little easier. But there’s one thing that’s often much harder to anticipate, especially on busy roads: cyclists. Waze is now looking to change that with a little help from Garmin. A few days ago, we reported that Waze was working with Garmin to make cyclists more visible to drivers. The two companies have now officially announced their partnership, bringing real-time cyclist alerts to Waze on both Android and iOS.

title: One UI 9.5 may introduce multiple new input options to Bixby widgets
summary: Meanwhile, Samsung Notes may pick up some visual upgrades with One UI 9.5.
body: TL;DR Samsung could give Bixby widgets a major upgrade with One UI 9.5, according to a new leak. While the number and size of the widgets will remain unchanged, they could gain new capabilities with the upcoming software. One UI 9.5 could also introduce some minor visual tweaks to the Samsung Notes app. Samsung’s One UI 9.5 could introduce an upgraded Bixby widget and bring visual changes to the Samsung Notes app, according to a new revelation. One UI 9.5 may be some distance away from launch, but we’re gradually learning about the changes it could bring, particularly to Samsung’s first-party apps. After yesterday’s revelation that One UI 9.5 could turn Bixby into an AI agent , another Bixby-related leak has now surfaced. In One UI 9, users can find a total of three Bixby widgets: 2×1, 2×2, and 4×2. While Samsung isn’t increasing that number or changing their sizes in One UI 9.5, it could make them more functional, per SamMobile’s reporting.

title: I ditched Google Chrome for Firefox for a week, and I finally see the appeal
summary: The fox was right all along.
body: Credit: Pankil Shah / Android Authority Chrome is one of the easiest browsers to pick up and use, but that simplicity comes at a cost. It takes half a dozen extensions, settings tweaks, and hidden flags to make Chrome do what browsers like Firefox already do out of the box. But the main reason I finally made the switch was privacy. Firefox is open-source, one of the few major non-Chromium browsers still standing. So I decided to test the waters and used it for a full week. Spoiler alert: I loved it.

title: I used the Pixel 11 Pro XL and Galaxy S26 Ultra for a week. This is the one I’d keep
summary: One flagship got the last laugh.
body: I have this habit of constantly comparing phones, even when I’m perfectly happy with the one I’m using. And when you have some of the best Android phones on the market sitting on your desk, it’s pretty hard to resist switching between them. So, instead of just comparing specs and calling it a day, I spent a week alternating between the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL and the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra to see which one I actually enjoyed using more. And after going back and forth between the two, I think I’ve finally found my favorite.

title: Hunter is killing Google Home and Alexa voice commands and automations in favor of Matter
summary: Existing smart fan controls face a January 1 deadline unless owners switch to Matter.
body: TL;DR Hunter is ending its legacy Google Home and Alexa cloud integrations on January 1, 2027, which will affect voice commands and automations. Matter will keep eligible HunterSMART fans connected, but some models will need firmware updates or replacement hardware. Physical controls and supported HunterSMART app features will continue working, although hardware upgrade costs and rollout timelines remain unclear. Matter is supposed to make smart homes less complicated, breaking down the walls between competing ecosystems and letting devices from different brands speak the same language. But for Hunter ceiling fan owners, getting everyone on the same page comes with an unexpected twist: the company is retiring the very connections that currently let its fans work with Google Home and Amazon Alexa . And there’s now a deadline attached. Hunter has been laying the groundwork for this change for months. The company started sending out emails in July (via Reddit ) revealing plans to bring Matter support to eligible smart ceiling fans, potentially through firmware updates or replacement Wi-Fi hardware.
